Lagos State Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, has urged youths to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and ensure they participate in the forthcoming polls, stressing that their votes would determine the country’s leadership. Hamzat, who is the governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the state, made the appeal at a youth mobilisation event organised by the Action Grassroots Alliance on Sunday. The event, tagged “Youth Mobilisation to Victory for PBAT and KOH 2027,” was organised to mobilise young voters for President Bola Tinubu and Hamzat ahead of the 2027 elections. Hamzat, who was represented by the Deputy Director-General of the state, Lagos State APC Campaign Council, Rasaq Olusola, particularly urged first-time voters to collect their PVCs and take part in the January and February elections. He said, “To the first-time voters, I want to appeal to you to ensure you take part in the January and February elections. The first step you need to take is to make sure you collect your Permanent Voter Cards. You must make sure you collect your PVCs so that you can have the opportunity to participate in the elections.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. He said, “To be a good ambassador of the APC, you must ensure you encourage your friends, your family and associates on the need to vote for the APC, because that is the only party that can address our challenges and attend to our problems.” The Director-General of the alliance, Salewa Adegbenro, said the group was targeting five million votes from Lagos youths for Tinubu and Hamzat ahead of the 2027 elections. 2027: APC targets Obi’s stronghold in Lagos Police arrest two over Kano APC chairman’s 68-day abduction Idris appoints ex-gov Dakingari Kebbi APC campaign DG Adegbenro disclosed this while speaking to journalists at the event, saying the alliance was embarking on door-to-door mobilisation to persuade young people to support the candidates. “We are looking at about five million votes from our youths because we are trying our best. We are doing our mobilisation and speaking to our people from door to door to ensure that they vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Dr Obafemi Kadri Hamzat in Lagos State,” she said. She said the alliance was mobilising young people because of their energy and capacity to influence national affairs. “The reason we are mobilising youths is that we know they are very energetic. We all know the capacity of youths, especially Gen Z, and their power to move nations. Our youths have the capacity to make things happen if they want to. That is why we are here today to encourage them and speak to them,” Salewa added. According to her, the alliance had established structures across the 20 local government areas and 37 local council development areas of Lagos State to drive its mobilisation. She added that the group was working with local government and council authorities to help eligible youths who had not yet obtained their PVCs.
